summary: Zero orphans both directions: 17 distinct declared check ids across cli-* equal the 17 CHECKS exports, verified by running the parser; the library is complete and fully reachable today.
The existing CI guard covers declared-to-implemented only; the reverse direction (a registry check no skill declares) is unguarded.
No adapter re-implements severity mapping, rule parsing, or dispatch shapes: all four preflights import the shared library, Cursor delegates to the Claude audit, OpenCode uses the shared core.
Realized drift #1: two dispatch-shape registries disagree on codex; the README's single-source-of-truth claim is already false, and the codex preflight/audit are inert as a result.
Realized drift #2: four model rosters exist as literal duplicates between executor-config.ts and fanout-run.cjs, and the codex builder default (o4-mini) disagrees with the packet default (gpt-5.5).
Realized drift #3: docs misstate the registry (README five-of-seventeen checks; availability comment says four above five implementations).

The fan-out builder satisfies stdin via process stdio, not a </dev/null token, so logged lineage commands would trip the stdin rule if pasted into a shell; a parity guard must treat spawn-level stdin as compliant.
sk-git is the anti-drift model: two transports import one GIT_CHECKS/GIT_SHAPE source and one evaluate/readHardRules engine.

Proposed single guard: table-driven shape-parity (both registries agree on one documented command per runtime) + bijection both directions + roster agreement; it would have caught every realized drift found.
